skill.name: format-standardize
skill.description: Standardize formatting and style for generated code, documentation, and written deliverables using project preferences and common formatting rules.
skill.summary: Applies consistent formatting rules to make generated deliverables ready for review or publication.
skill.author: AbeJitsu

content.value_statement: Generated work often has mixed spacing, headings, naming, or style choices. This skill applies consistent formatting standards so the final output is easier to review and publish.
actual_capabilities: Reviews generated deliverables for inconsistent formatting and style.
Applies saved formatting preferences through the documented StandardsRepository flow.
Standardizes code indentation, naming, spacing, imports, quotes, and semicolon style.
Standardizes documentation headings, lists, spacing, code blocks, links, and tables.
Reports the standards used, changes made, formatted deliverable, and validation result.
limitations: It depends on available project standards or user-provided formatting preferences.
It does not define a complete language-specific style guide by itself.
It may require external formatter tools when the user requests tool-based formatting.
It focuses on presentation consistency, not deep functional correctness.

use_cases.title: Prepare Code for Review
use_cases.description: Apply consistent indentation, naming, import order, and punctuation before a developer submits generated code.

use_cases.title: Polish Technical Documentation
use_cases.description: Normalize headings, lists, tables, links, and spacing before documentation is shared with a team.

use_cases.title: Finalize Client Deliverables
use_cases.description: Make mixed generated content follow one structure, tone, and visual format before delivery.

prompt_templates.title: Format a Short Draft
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner cleanup for a single generated answer.
prompt_templates.prompt: Standardize this deliverable using consistent headings, lists, spacing, and punctuation. Return the formatted version with a brief list of changes made.

prompt_templates.title: Apply Project Standards
prompt_templates.scenario: Use known project preferences for code or documentation.
prompt_templates.prompt: Load the project formatting standards and apply them to this generated deliverable. Include the standards used, changes made, final output, and validation result.

prompt_templates.title: Normalize Mixed Content
prompt_templates.scenario: Clean up a deliverable that combines code, prose, examples, and notes.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this mixed deliverable for inconsistent formatting across code, documentation, and explanatory content. Standardize each part while preserving meaning.

prompt_templates.title: Final Publication Pass
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced review before code review, release, or client delivery.
prompt_templates.prompt: Perform a final formatting pass against the saved standards and expected output format. Identify every formatting change and confirm the deliverable is ready for review.

output_examples.input: A generated documentation page has uneven heading levels, mixed bullet styles, and inconsistent spacing.
output_examples.output: The result uses a clear heading hierarchy, one bullet style, consistent blank lines, and a short validation summary.

output_examples.input: A generated component explanation includes inconsistent punctuation, import ordering notes, and unclear before-and-after sections.
output_examples.output: The result separates standards used, changes made, formatted content, and validation so reviewers can scan it quickly.

output_examples.input: A client handoff document mixes casual tone, irregular capitalization, and different list formats.
output_examples.output: The result uses one professional tone, consistent capitalization, aligned section structure, and readable lists.

best_practices: Provide the project style guide or saved standards before asking for final formatting.
Run the skill after content generation so it can polish a complete deliverable.
Review the listed changes to confirm formatting did not alter intended meaning.
anti_patterns: Do not use it as a substitute for functional testing or technical validation.
Do not ask it to invent standards when a project style guide already exists.
Do not mix unrelated deliverables in one pass when each needs different conventions.

faq.question: What does this skill standardize?
faq.answer: It standardizes code, documentation, refactoring notes, tests, and written content for consistent presentation.

faq.question: Can it use my project formatting rules?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill instructs the assistant to load saved standards and apply matching formatting preferences.

faq.question: Does it run formatters automatically?
faq.answer: It can follow user-requested tools such as Prettier or linters when those tools are available in the workflow.

faq.question: Will it change the meaning of my content?
faq.answer: It is intended to preserve meaning while improving formatting, structure, and consistency.

faq.question: Is it only for code?
faq.answer: No. It also covers documentation, tests, refactoring explanations, and general content creation.

faq.question: When should I use it?
faq.answer: Use it after generation and before review, publication, or delivery.
